scope: Nine curated examples for a catalog-first design prototype, not the full Awesome azd catalog or the approved production contract v1.

provenance.notes: Identity and original metadata were checked against the public catalog. Frameworks, requirements and features were enriched from linked repository READMEs or manifests, with record-level source notes. Task labels, concise titles, topics, best-fit guidance and conceptual flows are editorial proposals. Missing metadata stays explicit. No deployment, availability, cost or security validation is claimed.

templates.title: Chat with your documents
templates.subtitle: RAG with Azure AI Search + Python
templates.description: Build a conversational experience over your own documents, with search-grounded answers and citations.
templates.author: Azure Content Team
templates.bestFor: Teams exploring a Python document assistant with source citations and a ready-made chat interface.
features: Multi-turn chat with source citations.
Document ingestion and hybrid retrieval with Azure AI Search.
React frontend with optional authentication, speech and multimodal features.
Application Insights tracing and monitoring.
templates.architectureNote: Conceptual retrieval flow, not a deployment topology. Container Apps is the repository's default host; App Service is an alternative. Optional resources are not shown.
prerequisites: Azure subscription with roleAssignments/write and subscription-level deployments/write permissions; review the repository's existing-resource-group option for narrower access.
Azure Developer CLI, Git, Python 3.10-3.14 and Node.js 20+.
PowerShell 7+ on Windows. Verify regional model availability and quota before deploying.
templates.caveat: This is a reference sample, not a production security guarantee. Azure resources incur charges, including when a deployment is interrupted.
templates.sourceNote: Catalog, repository README, and app/frontend/package.json. The live AI catalog lists older Python and Node prerequisites; this study uses the repository requirements instead.

templates.title: Ask questions of your database
templates.subtitle: RAG on PostgreSQL
templates.description: Explore a RAG application that answers questions about rows in a PostgreSQL database.
templates.author: Azure Content Team
templates.bestFor: Developers who already think in relational tables and want to explore conversational access to PostgreSQL.
features: Hybrid retrieval using pgvector and PostgreSQL full-text search.
Optional function calling to translate questions into query filters.
React frontend and Python FastAPI backend.
Managed-identity access to Azure resources.
templates.architectureNote: Conceptual flow derived from the catalog description. Review the repository for the complete architecture and configuration.
prerequisites: Azure Developer CLI, Git, Node.js 18+ and Python 3.10+.
PostgreSQL 14+, pgvector and Docker Desktop for the local setup described in the README.
Azure subscription and adequate model quota; verify model availability in your target regions.
templates.caveat: Runtime requirements are summarized from the README; model quota, region support and costs still need checking. No deployment was performed.
templates.sourceNote: Canonical catalog and repository README, including the React/FastAPI architecture, prerequisites, costs and security guidance.

templates.title: Build a .NET knowledge assistant
templates.subtitle: RAG with Azure AI Search + C#
templates.description: Start a C# conversational app grounded in enterprise data, using Azure AI Search and Azure OpenAI.
templates.author: Azure Content Team
templates.bestFor: .NET teams evaluating a document-grounded assistant with a Blazor interface.
features: Blazor WebAssembly chat interface and ASP.NET Core Minimal API.
Semantic Kernel orchestration with Azure OpenAI and AI Search.
Citations and response-source inspection.
Voice, chat and question-answering interfaces.
templates.architectureNote: Conceptual retrieval flow, not a complete topology. The README explicitly identifies Container Apps as the default. The catalog also lists AKS; alternate deployment options require repository review.
prerequisites: Azure Developer CLI, .NET 8 SDK and Git.
Docker must be running during the documented provisioning/deployment workflow.
PowerShell 7+ on Windows and Azure permissions including roleAssignments/write. Check model quota and region availability.
templates.caveat: The default deployment provisions charge-incurring resources. Review security, region, model quota and the repository's deployment options before running.
templates.sourceNote: Canonical catalog and repository README. Default hosting, frameworks and prerequisites were cross-checked against the README; deployment was not tested.

templates.title: Bring document chat to Java
templates.subtitle: RAG with Azure AI Search + Java
templates.description: Explore the Java version of the enterprise-data chat sample with Azure OpenAI and AI Search.
templates.author: Davide Antelmo
templates.bestFor: Java teams exploring a microservice-based document assistant and choosing between Container Apps and AKS.
features: Spring Boot APIs and LangChain4j orchestration.
React chat with streaming answers and document citations.
Document upload, ingestion and search controls.
Container Apps and AKS deployment variants.
templates.architectureNote: Conceptual flow only. The current README describes Container Apps and AKS variants; no single default is assumed. The older catalog also lists App Service. Consult the deployment-specific guides.
templates.caveat: Prerequisites and default hosting are not verified in this study.
templates.sourceNote: Canonical catalog and current repository README. Frameworks reflect the current LangChain4j version; the earlier Semantic Kernel implementation lives on a separate branch.

templates.title: Give your agent new tools
templates.subtitle: Remote MCP with Azure Functions
templates.description: Build a remote Model Context Protocol server with TypeScript and Azure Functions.
templates.author: Paul Yuknewicz
templates.bestFor: Developers connecting an agent client to custom remote tools using the MCP protocol.
features: Separate examples for MCP tools, prompts and an interactive weather app.
TypeScript functions for remote tool endpoints.
Azure Functions bindings for integrating tools and storage.
templates.architectureNote: Conceptual flow. The current repository contains multiple samples; select a sample and follow its own README.
prerequisites: Node.js 18+ and Azure Functions Core Tools 4.0.7030 or later.
Azure Developer CLI and Docker for the local Azurite emulator.
Choose one sample directory and follow its own README; the root contains multiple independent samples.
templates.caveat: Setup needs repository review: its README now lists mcp-tools, mcp-prompts and mcp-weather-app. A root-level init command is intentionally not assumed.
templates.sourceNote: Catalog identity and IaC, plus the repository README. AI-tagged, but not marked as a member of the AI collection in the inspected catalog.

templates.title: Explore .NET Aspire + Storage
templates.subtitle: .NET Aspire Azure Storage Demo
templates.description: Try a .NET Minimal API with Azure Table Storage in an Aspire application on Container Apps.
templates.author: Frank Boucher
templates.bestFor: .NET developers learning Aspire orchestration, a Minimal API and Table Storage with a small sample application.
features: Employee-data endpoints backed by Azure Table Storage.
Local orchestration through the Aspire dashboard.
Storage-emulator integration for development.
OpenTelemetry observability.
templates.architectureNote: Conceptual flow from the catalog description; not a verified infrastructure diagram.
prerequisites: Docker Desktop or Podman for local development.
Azure Developer CLI for deployment; review Azure permissions and costs before provisioning.
templates.caveat: Community authorship is attribution, not a quality rating. Check the repository's prerequisites and costs.
templates.sourceNote: Canonical catalog, live Awesome azd init command and repository README. Local requirements and feature summaries come from the README.

templates.title: Build your first knowledge agent
templates.subtitle: Getting started with Microsoft Foundry agents
templates.description: Explore a web-based agent that retrieves knowledge from uploaded files, with citations, tracing and evaluation guidance.
templates.author: Azure Content Team
templates.bestFor: Developers who want to start with a Foundry-hosted knowledge agent rather than implement a retrieval pipeline from scratch.
features: File-search or AI Search knowledge retrieval with citations.
Built-in tracing, monitoring and evaluation examples.
Configurable model deployment and retrieval settings.
Codespaces, Dev Containers and local development guides.
templates.architectureNote: Conceptual interaction flow. The application runs on Container Apps and connects to Microsoft Foundry. Review the repository's diagram for all resources and identities.
templates.caveat: The README offers multiple deployment workflows. Choose one and review its RBAC, model quota and region requirements. This reference sample requires additional security work for production.
templates.sourceNote: Canonical catalog and repository README. The repository-supported Codespaces action is provided; a root init command and complete local prerequisites are not assumed.

templates.title: Start a Django web app
templates.subtitle: Django + PostgreSQL on App Service
templates.description: Build from a restaurant-review application with Django, PostgreSQL and a managed App Service host.
templates.author: Azure Content Team
templates.bestFor: Python developers looking for a conventional data-driven web app rather than an AI application.
features: Django restaurant-review application.
Managed PostgreSQL database.
App Service deployment instructions.
Dev Container configuration and local development guidance.
templates.architectureNote: Conceptual flow, not a network topology. The README describes App Service hosting and additional Redis integration options; confirm your selected infrastructure configuration.
templates.caveat: Follow the repository's fork/Codespaces or local setup workflow, then initialize the azd environment. Review database configuration, migrations and resource charges.
templates.sourceNote: Canonical catalog and repository README. Bicep is declared in the README front matter. Exact runtime requirements and a remote init action have not been independently confirmed.

templates.title: Bring your own app with Terraform
templates.subtitle: Azure Developer CLI Terraform starter
templates.description: Start with Terraform infrastructure modules and azd configuration, then add your own application code.
templates.author: Azure Dev
templates.bestFor: Developers who already have application code and want an infrastructure-first azd foundation.
features: Terraform module structure and provider configuration.
azd application and infrastructure configuration.
Dev Container tooling setup.
GitHub Actions and Azure Pipelines workflow assets.
templates.architectureNote: Conceptual workflow, not a preconfigured application topology. Hosting, databases and application language depend on the code and infrastructure you add.
prerequisites: Terraform 1.1.7 or later, Azure CLI and Azure Developer CLI.
An Azure subscription; review the README's Azure CLI authentication and subscription configuration.
Your own application code and Terraform resource configuration before application deployment.

templates.sourceNote: Canonical catalog and repository README. Tooling, provider requirements and workflow features are summarized from the README; no application language or default host is asserted.
